thread.title: Falcons fly past Flyers 42-7 - NewsBreak

author: Jeffrey Hage
title: Falcons fly past Flyers 42-7 - NewsBreak
text:
By Jeffrey Hage ,
7 days ago
The Little Falls Flyers gave up far too many big plays to the Foley Falcons in their Homecoming game on Friday, Sept. 19.
The result was a disappointing 42-7 home loss which dropped Little Falls’ record to 1-3 on the season.
“None of the three phases, offense, defense, special teams were successful,” Flyers’ head coach Joe Bartos said. “We were pretty disappointed coming off the football field. No one was injured, except for our pride. It was definitely a tough game to be a part of.”
Little Falls trailed 42-0 early in the fourth quarter when Nolan Sams caught a six-yard touchdown pass from Connor Neu.
It was a well designed and well executed play.
“Obviously down at the goal line, most teams would run, run, run, especially at the high school level,” Bartos said. “We executed a really nice fake and Nolan was open out in the flat. It was a nice, easy toss and catch.”
Neu finished the game 8-for-13 for 41 yards and an interception that was returned for a touchdown. His favorite target was Connor Pasterick, who had four receptions for 31 yards.
Liam Thoma led the Flyers with 36 rushing yards on 16 carries while Connor Neu had five carries for 29 yards and Ethan Neu rushed the ball eight times for 29 yards.
Defensively, the Flyers did a decent job against the run, allowing 96 yards on 24 carries. But Little Falls was torched for three TDs on just three passes and 175 yards.
“We’re really young and inexperienced in the defensive backfield coming into this year,” Bartos said. “We knew that and we’re going to see some changes, personnel-wise this week and we’ll do the same on offense as well. Guys are going to have some new opportunities to go out and play.”
Ethan Neu was the Flyers’ leading tackler with eight and he also recovered a red zone fumble (forced by Payton Bartos) to end a scoring chance. Foley also returned a kickoff for a TD.
Little Falls (1-3) played at undefeated Pierz (4-0) on Friday, Sept. 26, but no score was available at press time.
The Flyers will host the Albany Huskies in another tough matchup on Friday, Oct. 3. Kickoff is 7 p.m.
